transcript.text: I reviewed the university's master research agreement and the controlling schedule they supplied overnight. Background patents U1, U2, and U3 are licensed to the company only for noncommercial academic use. The current draft grants the university an exclusive commercial license to all background technology, which would improperly include those three patents. The final agreement must exclude U1, U2, and U3 from any commercial license and require separate written university consent before any commercial use of those patents. I have not yet incorporated this into the draft or circulated the finding, so the group is hearing it now for the first time.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Yesterday I held a working session with the product lead and privacy office, and we confirmed the company's non-negotiable clinical-data position: any publication of project results must prohibit patient-level data entirely, and all data must be de-identified before any permitted external publication. The working-session minutes have not yet been circulated to the deal team, so the group is hearing this now for the first time. This directly conflicts with the current draft's broad publication permission and needs to be reflected as a binding condition in the agreement before we go to the Legal Director.

decisions.background_ip_treatment: U1, U2, and U3 must be excluded from the exclusive commercial license granted to the university; the commercial license scope must be narrowed to exclude those three background patents.

commitments.detail: Revise the background technology license provisions to exclude U1, U2, and U3 from any commercial license and require separate written university consent before any commercial use of those patents.
Revise the publication provisions to prohibit patient-level data entirely and require de-identification of all data before any permitted external publication, as a binding condition in the agreement.

Upon confirmation that both revisions are incorporated into the draft, finalize the formal readout from IP Counsel and Privacy/Clinical Regulatory Counsel and proceed to approval decision per company policy.
